items.control_limits_en: 25th Dynasty (713–656 BCE): Shabaka 'brought the entire Nile valley as far as the Delta under the empire of Kush' (GHA2).
items.control_limits_ar: الأسرة الخامسة والعشرون (713–656 ق.م): «ضمّ شباكا وادي النيل كله حتى الدلتا إلى إمبراطورية كوش» (تاريخ أفريقيا العام II). [يحتاج تحقق]
items.notes: Two distinct extents: the 25th Dynasty maximum (c.713–656 BCE) and the post-593 BCE kingdom south of the Second Cataract. ZH_EMB_HIST2020 says Shabaka moved the capital to Memphis (popular text). Pass 16: sub-period reaches added under 'phases' (text only, low confidence; no geometry).

phases.label: Before the 25th Dynasty
phases.reach_en: No source read gives limits. GHA II says Kashta's Egyptian-style cartouches are on a stele found at Elephantine, from a time (c.−750) 'when the Nubians occupied at least part of Upper Egypt' (GHA2 ch.10, Leclant, p.280). Nothing on the southern reach for this sub-period, and nothing at all for the earliest rulers ('the names of the earliest rulers are unknown', p.279–80).

anchors.name: Elephantine (Kashta stele find-spot; not a border)

phases.label: After withdrawal from Egypt
phases.reach_en: 'In the far north, Lower Nubia, a kind of no man's land, remained in dispute between the Meroites and whoever were masters of Egypt' (GHA2 ch.10, pp.283–284); 'during the early part of the Napatan period Lower Nubia was for a considerable length of time entirely depopulated' and repopulated only from the 3rd/2nd c. BCE (GHA2 ch.11, Hakem, p.306). Southern limits: 'archaeological exploration has not been carried far enough … to indicate the limits … to the south'; accepted to include central Sudan 'at least as far as Sennar on the Blue Nile and Kosti on the White Nile' (GHA2 p.284) – a statement about the Kushite kingdom generally, NOT dated to 656–593.

items.control_limits_en: After the war with Rome (Treaty of Samos, 21/20 BCE) 'the frontier between the Roman and Meroitic empires was fixed at Hiera Sycaminos (Muharraqa)'; a Roman garrison at Primis (Qasr Ibrim) was later withdrawn (GHA2, ch.10). Naga is described as Meroe's southernmost city (NAGA_PROJ). Kush expanded south to around Khartoum (ZH_EMB_HIST2020, popular text).
items.control_limits_ar: بعد الحرب مع روما (معاهدة ساموس 21/20 ق.م) «ثُبّتت الحدود بين الإمبراطوريتين الرومانية والمروية عند هييرا سيكامينوس (المحرّقة)»، وسُحبت لاحقاً الحامية الرومانية من بريميس (قصر إبريم) (تاريخ أفريقيا العام II، الفصل 10). ويوصف النقعة بأنها أقصى مدن مروي جنوباً (مشروع النقعة). وتوسعت كوش جنوباً حتى منطقة الخرطوم (نص السفارة الصينية، نص شعبي).
items.notes: Northern frontier is well sourced (Samos). The southern and eastern limits are vague; the Naga 'southernmost city' claim is single-source and should be checked. Pass 16: sub-period reaches added under 'phases' (text only, low confidence; no geometry).

phases.label: Early Meroitic, before the Roman treaty
phases.reach_en: Reach of the kingdom (whole Napatan–Meroitic span, not dated more closely): 'from Lower Nubia to the south of Sennar and to Gebel Moya region in the southern Gezira plain and included extensive areas between the Nile valley and the Red Sea'; areas west of the Nile 'probably under Meroitic influence though their extent is still unknown' (GHA2 ch.11, Hakem, p.306). North: Philae and Dakka have 'sanctuaries of common Egyptian and Nubian dedication' under Ergamenes/Arkamani (late 3rd c. BCE) (GHA2 ch.10, p.287); the Dodecaschoenus (Aswan to Hiera Sycaminos) 'had belonged to the Ptolemies, but the rulers of Meroe … had long since added it to their kingdom' before Petronius' campaign (GHA2 p.209). The Samos frontier at Hiera Sycaminos dates from 21/20 BCE (end of this window). Lower Nubia repopulated only from the 3rd/2nd c. BCE (p.306), so a northern edge at Dakka/Maharraqa is defensible for the later part only.

items.control_limits_en: 'The kingdom of the Nobadae (Nuba in Arabic), known as Nobadia, extended from Philae to the Second Cataract. Its capital was Faras' (GHA2_CH12). Derda & Łajtar (2019) give Nobadia 'between the first and the third Nile cataracts', capital first at Qasr Ibrim and later Faras.
items.control_limits_ar: «امتدت مملكة النوباديين (النوبة بالعربية)، المعروفة بنوباتيا، من فيلة إلى الشلال الثاني، وكانت عاصمتها فرس» (تاريخ أفريقيا العام II، الفصل 12). ويحدد ديردا ولايتار (2019) نوباتيا «بين الشلالين الأول والثالث»، وكانت عاصمتها أولاً قصر إبريم ثم فرس.
items.notes: End of separate existence disputed: c.630 (Derda & Łajtar 2019), mid-7th c. (Maqrizi via GHA2_CH12), c.697 or later under Merkurios (GHA2_CH12), or late 6th c. (Godlewski hypothesis, via Derda & Łajtar). 700 is a placeholder.

items.control_limits_en: 'In the south, as far as ancient Meroe, another Nubian kingdom emerged in the sixth century with Old Dongola … as its capital' (GHA2_CH12); 'Entre la 3e et la 5e cataracte, se crée le royaume de Makouria, autour de la ville de Dongola' (FR_MUSEE_MEROE). 'Northern and Central Nubia united to form one state' (GHA2_CH12).
items.control_limits_ar: «وفي الجنوب، حتى مروي القديمة، نشأت في القرن السادس مملكة نوبية أخرى عاصمتها دنقلا العجوز» (تاريخ أفريقيا العام II، الفصل 12)؛ و«بين الشلالين الثالث والخامس نشأت مملكة المقرة حول مدينة دنقلا» (المتحف الفرنسي). ثم «اتحدت النوبة الشمالية والوسطى في دولة واحدة».
items.notes: The OHM relations carry no source tag; check them against the cited text before use. Two extents: before and after the union with Nobadia. OHM 2960090 (450–1265) reaches c.23.7°N, so it includes Nobadia's territory from 450, which conflicts with GHA2_CH12 (Nobadia was a separate kingdom from Philae to the Second Cataract until the union). Union with Nobadia: c.630 (Derda & Łajtar 2019) to c.697+ (Merkurios, GHA2_CH12); split the extent at the union with a disputed-date flag. Pass 16: sub-period reaches added under 'phases' (text only, low confidence; no geometry).

phases.label: Mamluk vassal kingdom
phases.reach_en: In 1276 Baybars's expedition defeated Dāwūd and gave the throne to Shakanda, who accepted terms 'that would practically have replaced the traditional bakt relationship by complete vassalage' (GHA4_CH16 p.403). Drawn as the existing GHA IV-derived 1276 shapes plus an Old Dongola marker.

phases.label: Kings at al-Daw (Maris)
phases.reach_en: 1365–6: king moved to al-Daw in Maris, Dunkula left in ruins (GHA4 p.404). Not an end: 'the Nubian kings retained their residence at al-Daw'; last written reference to the Nubian king 1397 (GHA4_CH16 p.404). Marker at al-Daw (db/cities.json, Q1496812); identification with Gebel Adda VERIFY. No cited reach is drawn.

items.control_limits_en: 'Nubia was therefore a Christian country consisting of three kingdoms: Nobadia in the north, Makuria in the centre and Alodia in the [south]' (GHA2_CH12). Alodia lay 'in the heartland of the old Kushite kingdom', capital Soba (ZH_EMB_HIST2020: 位于古库西提克王国中心地带…首都在索巴).
items.control_limits_ar: «كانت النوبة إذن بلداً مسيحياً من ثلاث ممالك: نوباتيا في الشمال، والمقرة في الوسط، وعلوة في [الجنوب]» (تاريخ أفريقيا العام II، الفصل 12). وكانت علوة «في قلب مملكة كوش القديمة» وعاصمتها سوبا (نص السفارة الصينية).
items.notes: No boundary is stated. The GHA2 sentence is cut at a page break ('Alodia in the'), so [south] is my completion.

items.control_limits_en: 'Upper Nubia, above the Third Cataract, was under the suzerainty of the Funj rulers', while Lower Nubia (First to Third Cataract) was 'nominally at least' dependent on Ottoman Egypt (HD2011). 'Kordofan was a debatable land between the rulers of Sennar and Darfur' (HD2011). By 1523 the Funj sultanate reached north to Dongola, and after 1585 Hannik, south of the Third Cataract, became the Funj–Ottoman border (ZH_EMB_HIST2020).
items.control_limits_ar: «كانت النوبة العليا، فوق الشلال الثالث، تحت سيادة حكام الفونج»، بينما كانت النوبة السفلى (من الشلال الأول إلى الثالث) تابعة «اسمياً على الأقل» لمصر العثمانية (هولت وديلي). و«كانت كردفان أرضاً متنازعاً عليها بين حكام سنار ودارفور». وبحلول 1523 امتدت سلطنة الفونج شمالاً حتى دنقلا، وبعد 1585 صارت حنّيك جنوب الشلال الثالث حدّاً بين الفونج والعثمانيين (نص السفارة الصينية).
items.notes: Sennar anchored to Wikidata Q611867 / GeoNames 367644. The capital in 1821 (old Sennar) may not coincide exactly with the modern town; flagged. Southern and eastern limits (Fazughli, Ethiopian marches) were not found in the sources read (HD2011 intro pp.1–9 only); still open.

items.control_limits_en: West: wars with Wadai 'ended in stalemate', with tension 'usually caused by the machinations of the tributary states along the border, Qimr, Tama, or Sila' (OFAHEY2018_FWD). Al-Tunisi (as reported by Takana) put the borders 'from al-Tuwaisha in the east to the last point in Dar Masalit in the west'; south: 'the empty land between the Fur sultanate and Dar Firteet'; north: from al-Mazroob, with Zaghawa, Midob and Barti as affiliated kingdoms (TAKANA2016, p.9). East/Kordofan: before c.1785 Kordofan was 'a vast area west of the White Nile under no central rule' (OFAHEY2018_FWD) and 'a debatable land between the rulers of Sennar and Darfur' (HD2011). 'Darfur rule over Kordofan was to last just under forty years (1785–1821)'; Darfur and Kordofan together 'covered some 866,000 square kilometers' (OFAHEY2018_FWD). Kordofan was lost when Musallim was killed at Bara on 19 Aug 1821 (OFAHEY2018_FWD); the Kayra 'ruled Darfur until 1874' (GHA6_CH14).
items.control_limits_ar: الغرب: انتهت الحروب مع وداي «إلى طريق مسدود»، وكان التوتر ينشأ «عادةً من مكائد الدول التابعة على الحدود: القِمر والتاما والسيلا» (أوفاهي 2018). وبحسب التونسي (كما ينقل تكنة) امتدت حدود السلطنة «من الطويشة في الشرق إلى آخر نقطة في دار مساليت في الغرب»؛ وجنوباً «الأرض الخالية بين سلطنة الفور ودار فرتيت»؛ وشمالاً من المزروب، مع ممالك تابعة هي الزغاوة والميدوب والبرتي (تكنة 2016، ص9). الشرق/كردفان: قبل نحو 1785 كانت كردفان «منطقة شاسعة غرب النيل الأبيض لا تخضع لحكم مركزي» (أوفاهي 2018) و«أرضاً متنازعاً عليها بين حكام سنار ودارفور» (هولت وديلي). و«دام حكم دارفور لكردفان قرابة أربعين عاماً (1785–1821)»، وغطّت دارفور وكردفان معاً «نحو 866 ألف كيلومتر مربع» (أوفاهي 2018). وضاعت كردفان بمقتل مسلّم في بارا في 19 أغسطس 1821؛ و«حكم الكيرا دارفور حتى 1874» (تاريخ أفريقيا العام VI).
items.notes: Two extents: core Darfur (c.1640–1874; start follows the era date, GHA V ch.7 pp.187–188) and Darfur plus Kordofan (1785–1821). O'Fahey 2008 was not read (table of contents only; frontiers chapter p.178), so it is listed as further reading, not as the basis for any phrase. OFAHEY2018_FWD was read through the search index only. The foreword says Tayrab led the army into Kordofan 'in the early 1780s' and also gives 1785 as the start of Darfur rule. The al-Tunisi borders describe c.1803–11 and reach us at second hand via Takana. Place names al-Tuwaisha, Dar Firteet and al-Mazroob have no Wikidata coordinates, so they are not anchored. The earlier ZH_EMB_HIST2020 phrase was replaced with scholarly sources. Pass 14 frontier anchors: al-Tuwaisha resolved (OSM node 7730407134); Geneina, Dar Masalit and Dar Fertit are region/centre points only. al-Mazroob is UNRESOLVED: al-Tunisi calls it 'the first water well that meets those coming from the Egyptian border' (TAKANA2016 p.9), but OSM has only same-name settlements that don't fit: node 7730430502 (13.9019, 29.3194, West Bara, North Kordofan), node 13355388871 (11.5789, 26.9764, Adila, East Darfur), node 11119507330 'Mazrub' (13.5366, 22.8861, Kirendik, West Darfur), node 7731805418 'Mazrūb' pond (10.6167, 28.1167, West Kordofan). GeoNames could not be queried (API unreachable). Not anchored.

anchor_sites.name: Salima (Selima) Oasis – route junction, not a border

items.control_limits_en: In 1821 the lands 'from Nubia to the Ethiopian foothills and from the Atbara to Darfur' became part of Muhammad Ali's empire (ZH_EMB_HIST2020: 从努比亚至衣索比亚山麓和从阿特巴拉河至达尔富尔). Darfur was held by the Kayra until 1874 (GHA6_CH14). In Equatoria, Baker and Gordon 'were unable to extend Turkish administration … beyond a few scattered posts' (GHA6_CH14).
items.control_limits_ar: في 1821 صارت الأراضي «من النوبة إلى سفوح الحبشة ومن نهر عطبرة إلى دارفور» جزءاً من إمبراطورية محمد علي (نص السفارة الصينية). وظلت دارفور بيد الكيرا حتى 1874 (تاريخ أفريقيا العام VI). وفي الاستوائية «عجز بيكر وغوردون عن مدّ الإدارة التركية إلى أبعد من بضع نقاط متناثرة».
items.notes: OHM 2690845 'Turco-Egyptian Sudan' (1820–1867), no source tag. Its polygon reaches c.22.3°E, so it includes Darfur, which conflicts with GHA6_CH14 (Darfur held by the Kayra until 1874). OHM 2690836 (Khedivate of Egypt) was dropped because it covers Egypt only. Extents grow in stages: 1821, then Taka/Kassala, Equatoria posts, Darfur 1874. Pass 16: OHM 2690845 tags (checked 2026-10-20) carry no source tag, and colony_of=Britain is wrong for 1820–67; its north-west corner is unsourced. Scholarly statements found: GHA VI ch.14 (Ibrahim, p.372) gives the extent only at the end of the period – 'from the second cataract to the equatorial lakes and from the Red Sea to Darfur', Darfur being added under Ismail (1874). HD2011 (intro, pp.8–9) places Darfur's frontier-post at Suwayna on the Darb al-Arba'in, which met the Nile route at the Salima (Selima) Oasis (Wikidata Q85800315, 21.3667N 29.3167E) – that describes the pre-1820 route, not a Turkiyya border. No source read gives a north-western limit for 1821–1874. Recommendation: before 1874 clip the western edge at Darfur's eastern border (Kordofan was taken in 1821, Darfur only in 1874) and do not draw anything into the Libyan desert; mark the north-west edge 'unsourced'.

items.control_limits_en: After Shaykan (1883) the Mahdists controlled Kordofan, Darfur and Bahr al-Ghazal; 'Uthman Digna took the east except Sawakin (Suakin)' (GHA7_CH4). Losses: Tushki 1889, Tokar 1891, Kassala 1894 (GHA7_CH4).

items.control_limits_en: 'From January 1899 Eastern Sudan was declared a joint possession (condominium) of Great Britain and Egypt and in effect turned into a British colony' (BRE_AES). Darfur's 'dynastic Muslim state … was not finally extinguished until 1916' (HD2011), so Darfur lay outside direct control until 1916.
items.control_limits_ar: «منذ يناير 1899 أُعلن السودان الشرقي ملكاً مشتركاً (حكماً ثنائياً) لبريطانيا العظمى ومصر، وتحوّل فعلياً إلى مستعمرة بريطانية» (الموسوعة الروسية الكبرى). ولم «تنطفئ نهائياً» دولة الفور المسلمة «حتى 1916» (هولت وديلي)، فظلت دارفور خارج السيطرة المباشرة حتى ذلك العام.
items.notes: OHM Anglo-Egyptian Sudan series: 1899-06-19→1902, 1902→1910-06-10, 1910-06-10→1912, 1912→1934, 1934→1956-01-01, all without source tags. CShapes 2.0 also covers dependencies from 1886, but it is CC BY-NC-SA, so do not use it for shapes. halaib.start_note: Administrative line made by arrêté of 25 Jul 1902 and decree of 4 Nov 1902 (IBS18_1962 p.3); the 22nd-parallel political line dates from the 19 Jan 1899 Agreement (p.2). The territory becomes a two-sided dispute at independence in 1956 (WP_HALAIB); first open crisis: Egyptian note of 1 Feb 1958, plebiscite set for 21 Feb 1958 (IBS18_1962 p.5).
halaib.recommend: Draw 'Sudan-administered north of 22°N' 1902–1958; 'disputed' 1958–present (Egypt's note of 1 Feb 1958, IBS18_1962 p.5 and UN S/3963; no formal Egyptian protest in 1956, IBS fn.9; 1956 appears only in later claims – Analyst check, db/halaib_dates_check.md); 'Egyptian control (effective)' from 1995 (medium; other dates in sources: presence 1992–93, full control 1994 per Carnegie, Jan 2000 per Al Jazeera Arabic/EGYPIL) (expulsion of Sudanese police after the June 1995 Addis Ababa attempt on Mubarak); Sudanese forces withdrew Jan 2000. 1990s dates are Wikipedia-only (citing Ofcansky 2002 p.985), flagged. WP_HALAIB also says 'in 1994 the Egyptian military moved to take control', and elsewhere 'under Egyptian administration since mid-1990' – inconsistent; use 1995 with a note.

bir_tawil.start_note: Egypt-administered area south of 22°N under the 1902 line (IBS18_1962 pp.3–4; Ababda grazing). Unclaimed by either state from 1956 on (WP_BIRTAWIL).
bir_tawil.recommend: Draw 'Egypt-administered south of 22°N' 1902–1958; 'claimed by neither state' 1958–ongoing (start year inferred from Egypt's 1958 note, medium; unclaimed status confirmed by Britannica and Pinkerton 2014 – Analyst check, db/halaib_dates_check.md).
